title: Text Size and Weight
context: Why large and bold text has a lower contrast threshold
whyItMatters: Larger, thicker letterforms can be easier for the eye to resolve, allowing a lower contrast threshold.
learningObjectives: Recognize how text size affects visual perception.
Identify the 3:1 target for large text.
Define the size breakpoints used for large text.
lessonParagraphs: Small, thin text needs a stronger difference from its background to remain clear. A large, bold headline has more visible surface area, so its shapes can be easier for the eye to resolve.
The research describes a 3:1 target for large text and a 4.5:1 target for standard text. The lower threshold for large text is tied to how its larger or thicker letterforms are perceived.
Text is considered large at 24 pixels in a regular weight, or about 18.5 pixels when bold. Below those dimensions, the standard text target applies.
Size-based thresholds offer room for expressive color choices in prominent text while keeping smaller details easier to read.
